item.title: Houthis say hit two Saudi ports in response to coalition strikes
item.description:
Yemen's Houthis said Wednesday they had targeted the Saudi ports of Jeddah and Jazan in response to Saudi strikes on a Yemeni port controlled by the Iran-backed group as their conflict further escalated.

The attacks came after the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said it had struck Yemen's Red Sea port city of Hodeida, drawing threats of retaliation from the Yemeni fighters.

"Both operations resulted in damage to the targeted sites," Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said.

item.title: Israeli judges recommend prosecutors drop one bribery case against Netanyahu
item.description:
JERUSALEM, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Israeli judges on Wednesday recommended that prosecutors drop one of three long-running cases against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and reconsider another alleging he granted favours in exchange for positive media coverage.

Netanyahu was indicted in 2019 on charges of bribery, fraud and breach of trust. He denies the charges and has pleaded not guilty. His trial began in 2020 and involves three criminal cases.

item.title: Thirty-one killed in fire after vehicle overturns in Egypt
item.description:
By Enas Alashray and Yomna Ehab

CAIRO, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Thirty-one people were killed and 21 wounded in a fire after a vehicle carrying petroleum products overturned on a major ring road in Egypt, authorities said on Wednesday.

The fire broke out above a tunnel in Giza's Al-Warraq district, the public prosecution said. Preliminary estimates found that 27 vehicles, including cars and motorcycles, had been charred, it said, adding that casualty figures and damage were still being assessed.

item.title: Egypt says 30 dead in Cairo fire after fuel truck overturns
item.description:
A fire erupted in Egyptian capital Cairo on Wednesday killing at least 30 people, according to the health ministry, after a fuel truck reportedly overturned on a packed highway.

AFP footage showed a huge fireball and thick black smoke rising above the densely populated capital's Al-Waraq neighbourhood as motorists sounded their horns and scrambled to get away. Surrounding buildings appeared to escape the flames.

item.title: UK is moving military aircraft to hangars at night over possible drone threats, media reports say
item.description:
LONDON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Britain's Royal Air Force is moving aircraft to hangars and shelters at night to protect them from possible drone threats, British media reported on Wednesday.

The Times newspaper and Sky News, which both reported the measures without citing sources, said they also included plans to use anti-drone netting to protect exposed aircraft.
